HNB Stockbrokers
News highlights 16th November 2026

_LOCAL NEWS_🇱🇰

Institutional analysts say Budget 2027 broadly toes fiscal line, warn of post-IMF tests
HNB Stockbrokers said the primary surplus just meets the IMF target. It warned that the margin for error narrows once the EFF ends and Sri Lanka is likely to return to international Bond markets. “Continued fiscal discipline remains key to sustaining improving fiscal dynamics and building buffers with a view to securing credit rating upgrades as the IMF program comes to an end, particularly in the backdrop of heightened external risks,” it said. HNB Stockbrokers noted that Sri Lanka’s term premium remains elevated against higher-rated peers, which would raise the cost of new borrowing.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/zjf9xrsv

Annual Borrowing Plan: No ISB in 2027, bilateral borrowing instead
Sri Lanka is to avail of bilateral and multilateral borrowings in 2027, despite its constrained options in accessing low-interest loans with international financing agencies in the medium term, and with its Annual Borrowing Plan making no arrangement for an ISB issuance in 2027.
Describing Sri Lanka's narrowing options to avail of cheaper borrowing through bilaterals and multilaterals, due its graduation into a Upper Middle Income status by the World Bank, the report said: "As Sri Lanka has been upgraded…the availability of concessional financing from the external bilateral and multilateral agencies will gradually become more limited over the medium term."
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/yse32fky

LAUGFS Price Hike: No MRP, no legal action?
Despite the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) summoning LAUGFS Gas PLC officials over the company’s recent domestic gas price hike, there is no possibility of taking legal action over the increase unless domestic gas is brought under the maximum retail price (MRP) regime, it is learnt.The CAA has however summoned LAUGFS officials to appear before the Authority on the 16th of November to explain the recent price increase.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/4829vae9

Tourism earnings rise for third consecutive month in October, but 10-month revenue remains down 8.3%
Sri Lanka’s tourism earnings registered a third consecutive monthly increase in October, rising 3.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $ 192.7 million, after recording its highest-ever monthly tourist arrivals during the month, welcoming 168,625 visitors as demand strengthened ahead of the winter season, according to the latest data released by the Central Bank. However, the latest monthly gain has yet to reverse the broader weakness in the sector. Tourism earnings during the first 10 months of 2026 fell 8.3% YoY to $ 2.43 billion, compared with $ 2.65 billion in the corresponding period last year. 
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/4nmhzr2t

Seafood exporters hail Budget 2027, eye $ 680 m by 2030
The Seafood Exporters’ Association of Sri Lanka (SEASL) yesterday said it “strongly supports” the Government’s 2027 Budget proposals, recognising their potential to accelerate investment, expand value-added seafood processing, strengthen sustainable fisheries and improve Sri Lanka’s international competitiveness.SEASL believes Sri Lanka has the potential to achieve $ 680 million in annual seafood export earnings by 2030, provided the industry is supported by sustained investment, greater value addition, modern infrastructure and efficient trade policies.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/5fb7v368

_Global NEWS_🌍

Yen steady against euro and dollar after soft Japanese GDP data
he yen was pinned near two-month lows against the dollar and little moved against the euro in early trade on Monday as markets assessed how an unexpected contraction in the Japanese economy in the third quarter affects the policy outlook. The yen ‌fluctuated between gains and losses without moving too far, trading against the dollar at 159.69 yen and against the euro at 176.04 yen, close to levels where US and Japanese authorities are believed to have intervened earlier this year.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/mrbmw3au

US diesel below $6 a gallon at 2-month low on easing tensions, weaker demand
US diesel prices fell below $6 a gallon on average on Saturday after two months above that threshold, retreating from record highs as easing geopolitical tensions and seasonal demand weakness reduce pressure on fuel markets. Diesel had surged ‌as the US-Israeli war against Iran disrupted oil supplies and Ukraine's systematic attacks on Russian refineries stymied production. Elevated diesel prices, a key driver of transportation and freight costs, have boosted overall inflation, causing pain for consumers, farmers and businesses. High fuel costs were a major factor helping Democrats sweep both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republicans ⁠in this month's midterm elections.
